def: A system in which models and tools are orchestrated through predefined code paths that you write, rather than the model choosing its own next step.
Splitting a task into a fixed sequence of model calls in which each call processes the previous one's output, trading latency for accuracy.
A programmatic check between two steps of a workflow that decides whether to continue, so that bad output stops cheaply instead of propagating.
Classifying an input and sending it down a specialised path, with its own prompt, tools or model, plus a fallback for low confidence.
A parallelisation variant in which independent subtasks of one job run at the same time and their results are combined in code.
A parallelisation variant in which the same task runs several times and the answers are combined, usually by majority, to raise confidence.
A pattern in which a central model call decides the subtasks from the specific input, workers handle them, and a final call synthesises the results.
A loop in which one call produces a draft, another checks it against criteria and returns feedback, and the producer revises until the check passes or a limit is reached.
Mistakes that several judges or runs make together on the same hard items, which cap the accuracy gain from voting however many votes you add.
The chain of steps whose durations determine how long a run takes, so that parallel work off the path adds tokens but not waiting time.
